summary.zh: 唯一存活的银杏目植物，扇形叶、秋季金黄，是东亚寺庙与街道的标志树。
summary.en: The sole survivor of an ancient order; fan-shaped leaves that turn gold in autumn make it an icon of East Asian temples and avenues.

field_marks.zh: 叶扇形，中央常有缺刻（biloba＝两裂），叶脉二叉状，无主脉。雌树秋季结黄色种子，外种皮腐熟后有强烈异味。
field_marks.en: Fan-shaped leaves often notched in the middle (biloba = two-lobed) with dichotomous veins and no midrib. Female trees bear yellow seeds in autumn whose fleshy coat smells strongly when ripe.

similar.zh: 与枫、悬铃木的区别：银杏叶无主脉、叶脉从叶柄呈扇状分叉。
similar.en: Unlike maples or plane trees, ginkgo leaves have no midrib; veins fan out from the stalk.

story.zh: 银杏所属谱系可追溯到二叠纪，侏罗纪时分布极广。今天的银杏只有一种，被称为‘活化石’。全基因组草图显示其基因组很大，约 10 Gb，并保留了古老的基因家族。
story.en: The lineage reaches back to the Permian and was widespread in the Jurassic. Today one species remains — a 'living fossil'. Its draft genome is large (~10 Gb) and retains ancient gene families.

notes.zh: 秋季叶片转金黄约在 10 月下旬至 12 月初（随纬度推迟）。雌树落果时请避开，气味刺鼻且果肉可能引起皮肤过敏。
notes.en: Leaves turn gold from late October to early December depending on latitude. Avoid fallen female seeds: the smell is pungent and the pulp can irritate skin.
